question: A 62-year-old woman with a third-degree uterovaginal prolapse wishes surgical correction. She has no history of previous pelvic surgery or malignancy. Uterine size is normal on examination. Which surgical approach is most appropriate?

answers.text: Vaginal hysterectomy with anterior and posterior colporrhaphy (pelvic floor repair)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Vaginal hysterectomy combined with anterior and posterior colporrhaphy is the standard surgical treatment for symptomatic uterovaginal prolapse in the absence of contraindications. The vaginal route directly addresses the prolapsed compartments and avoids an abdominal incision.
Incorrect. TAH does not address the pelvic floor defects responsible for prolapse. Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair is the appropriate procedure for prolapse correction.

Incorrect. While sacrocolpopexy is used for vault prolapse after hysterectomy, the primary surgical treatment for uterovaginal prolapse is vaginal hysterectomy plus colporrhaphy. Laparoscopic mesh procedures are more complex and not the standard first-line for straightforward prolapse.

answers.text: Pelvic floor physiotherapy and ring pessary only, because surgery is too risky at age 62

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Age 62 alone is not a contraindication to surgery for prolapse. Conservative management (pessary, physiotherapy) is appropriate for those who decline surgery or are unfit, but surgical correction is appropriate and commonly performed in fit women of this age.

overallFeedback.feedback: Vaginal hysterectomy combined with pelvic floor repair (anterior/posterior colporrhaphy) is the standard operation for symptomatic uterovaginal prolapse.
Correct. Third-degree prolapse with normal uterine size and no contraindications = vaginal hysterectomy + anterior and posterior colporrhaphy.
